utterances.text: General, if Colonel Blagojevic realised that he was sending this document to the Command of the operative group in Zepa, why did he not say that in the order? Why did he not address it to the forward command post of the Operative Group Zepa?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Because it was the forward command post of the Drina Corps which conducted the operation, and the forward command post was established as the point from which the commander involved in the Zepa operation would carry out his command, and that is the reason why forward command posts are established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you yourself have said, and I've reminded you on a number of occasions, you've said that the forward command post is the place from which the commander of the corps fights the battle. Now, if that principle holds true, General, Colonel Blagojevic was sending this to General Krstic at the forward command post of the Drina Corps because he believed that General Krstic was the Commander of the Drina Corps, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: No. He knew exactly that General Krstic was not yet the Commander of the Drina Corps but that he was the Commander of the group which was conducting the Zepa operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can have Prosecutor's Exhibit 537, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, you've stated in your evidence that you have not come across a single document in which the Main Staff authorised the Drina Corps to task or monitor the activities of Main Staff units. Do you recall that evidence? Do you recall that evidence, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. I haven't quite understood you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall stating to this courtroom that you have not come across a single document in which the Main Staff authorised the Drina Corps to task or monitor the activities of Main Staff units?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: To issue tasks to the units of the Main Staff, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this is an order which is from Colonel Ignjat Milanovic. It is addressed, as you can see, to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Actually, in the English version, Your Honours, there is a typographical error on it which it has not been corrected yet but you should ignore where it says, "delivered for the command" because in fact on the original version of it says, "To: The forward command post," and then underneath that to the "Drina Corps Command." General, who was Colonel Ignjat Milanovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Colonel Ignjat Milanovic was the Chief of Air Defence with the Staff of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you will see, General, that Colonel Milanovic is addressing this particular report to the corps forward command post. He is making this document for the attention of the commander. He is also copying it to the Drina Corps Command. Now, you would agree with me that if Colonel Milanovic, a staff officer within the Drina Corps, was addressing a document to the commander of the corps forward command post, he believed that General Krstic was the Commander of the Drina Corps, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't agree with you. Colonel Milanovic knew exactly who was at the forward command post and who was commanding the forces from that forward command post. That was General Krstic, and it was sent to him, this document. And this document is not an order, it's a proposal. He doesn't have authority to order the commander. He can only submit his proposals to the Commander of the Operative Group who is expecting the forces engaged in the search of the terrain to report to him so they can be deployed for the Zepa operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, you'll see that in this document, Colonel Milanovic is stating, "In accordance with your orders I went to Milici and Bratunac." He says that, I think you will see, in the first paragraph. And then he states underneath, "I have ordered: 1. General mobilisation to be carried out in Bratunac, Milici, Vlasenica, and Sekovici. 2. The assignment you have given to the commanders to be carried out without fail." Now, General, on the basis that Milanovic is stating that he is acting according to Krstic's orders, you would agree with me that General Krstic is giving orders in respect of operations that have absolutely nothing to do with what is going on in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with you. This is a continuation of the order which was issued for the search of the terrain to the Bratunac and Milici Brigades and the Skelani Battalion. Colonel Milanovic, as per the authorisation of General Krstic, went to the field to check out on what was going on and why those forces were not coming to Zepa because he expected them there. He expected that they would be engaged for the purposes of the Zepa operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now. General, you will see at the bottom of this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And Mr. Usher, if you could move the document up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- there is a proposal from Colonel Milanovic, and you will see that the proposal is to authorise and appoint the commander of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade as commander of all forces are participating in searching the terrain and sweeping the battlefield. Now, General, General Krstic in his evidence to this Court in being questioned by my learned friend Mr. McCloskey was asked the question, "Do you know if you accepted his proposal and acted upon it?" General Krstic's response was, "I accepted his proposal regarding Colonel Blagojevic that he should be appointed commander, the commander to be in charge of the search of the terrain in the area." Were you aware, General, that General Krstic had accepted this proposal in this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now have Prosecutor's Exhibit 469.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, you've seen this document before, and this is the document in respect of General Zivanovic, and you stated in your evidence in-chief, that being in response to a Judge's question, that you were not aware of Zivanovic taking up any significant posts after the 15th of July. Do you recall stating that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you will see it says very clearly on this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And Mr. Usher, if you could refer to, I think, the next page of that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will see it says very clearly that General Zivanovic was placed on disposal. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that means essentially, doesn't it, General, that General Zivanovic was not moving on to any other position after he was removed from the Drina Corps command, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't mean that, what you're saying. It means that as of the 15th, that is, from the 15th, which is the earliest date when General Zivanovic may step from his duty -- step down from his duty as the corps commander, and that is also the earliest date when the personnel service can count on General Zivanovic for new appointments. This is a phrase which is used in terms of personnel matters, human resources matters, for all commanding officers who are thereby relieved of their previous duties and are placed on disposal for further appointments. It is therefore possible to -- for them to be appointed to a new post in the same document, but they can also be placed at disposal until some new appointment. But this is the earliest date when they may step down from their duty in accordance with the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, General --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: And this is in accordance with the document on the appointment of General Krstic for the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To what position was General Zivanovic appointed to by virtue of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: I have just answered that, but I will repeat myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: The expression that he's made available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was General Zivanovic appointed to any substantive position as a result of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: As a result of this document, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, it's correct, isn't it, that General Zivanovic never occupied any position after this date, any position of which you have already said you were aware? You are not aware that he occupied any significant position, are you, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that he was appointed to any substantive position because probably that would have been indicated in this same document, if that is what they had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I could have Prosecutor's Exhibit 539, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this particular document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this is a daily combat report from the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, Colonel Blagojevic, and what I am particularly interested in is the second paragraph of that document where it says about halfway down, "During the day the Brigade commander visited all units which are blocking the enemy retreat (the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, units of the 65th Protection Motorised Regiment, part of the MUP, and the 5th Engineering Battalion) defined their tasks and organised their joint action and communication." Now, General, we have just been considering the previous document in which General Krstic approves of Milanovic's proposal to appoint the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade in command of all of the forces participating in the search, and you would agree with me that here the Brigade Commander, Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic, is reporting back that he is coordinating the activities of all of the units blocking the retreat, including the 65th Protection Motorised Regiment, parts of the MUP, and the other units referred to. That's what he's doing, isn't he, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: He does not say that he is supervising the 65th Protection Regiment, but he's only reporting that he toured them, and as they are close to the area of responsibility, there's no harm in that, but he's not stating that he is coordinating --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I'm going to interrupt you because that is not what the report says. The report says that the Commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade defined their tasks and organised their joint action and communications. You would agree with me, General, that Colonel Blagojevic is stating that he defined the tasks of the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment and parts of the MUP in accordance with General Krstic's order. That's what he's doing, isn't he, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: No. Colonel Blagojevic's obligations towards the 65th Protection Regiment are indicated in the next sentence, and they have to do with coordination and not supervision. There's no document that places the 65th Regiment under the authority of the commander. There is no document from the Main Staff or the Drina Corps towards the Bratunac Brigade, and also it is quite contrary to the principles of doctrine. There are two facts against it: There is no document to show it, number one; and number two, it is contrary to doctrine. So this relates only to joint action. He toured them, familiarised himself for what they were doing, and he told the head of the Protection Regiment what they were doing, and beyond that, he has no further authority over the 65th Regiment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, in Prosecutor's Exhibit 407/a which is "Rules of Ground Forces," let me just quote you paragraph 63 since you've mentioned doctrine. "Command and control. General provisions. Command and control Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. are conscious and organised activities of the commander of the corps and of the bodies of command aimed at engaging and unifying the actions and activities of all units." General, it's a fundamental principle, isn't it, in the JNA, in the VRS, that units that are doing the same tasks are coordinated by the one command. That is a fundamental principle, isn't it, General, as referred to in your rules?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Yes, but that does not apply to this order here. You have an order the very next day appointing Keserovic to coordinate activities. The very next day you have another document which says that a provisional command is being formed which will unified activities from the 17th to the 19th in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get to that document in a moment. When this document states that the Commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade was defining the tasks and organising the joint actions of the MUP and the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment, that means exactly what it says, doesn't it, that those units were placed under his command for the purposes of this operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: No. No, sir. When a superior wants to place a unit under a certain command, then he explicitly says so in a command document, saying, "We're placing at your disposal the 65th Protection Regiment for the execution of tasks along such-and-such axis in such-and-such an area until such-and-such a date," and only then can the brigade commander have control of that unit. In this way, his obligation was simply to organise the joint action of his units toward them. He has no authority over the 65th Regiment. He was given no such authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you stating to the Judges that in essence Colonel Blagojevic is reporting back to the Drina Corps that he was defining tasks and organising joint action knowing full well that he had absolutely no authority over those units at all? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: My evidence is exactly what is stated there, to organise --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: -- joint action and to issue orders to his units, his own units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, isn't this document stating that Colonel Blagojevic believed that he had the capacity to define the tasks of the MUP and the 65th Protection Regiment? Isn't this what this document says?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: No. He specifies the tasks of his own units and organises joint action with other units which are not under his command, because if they were under his command, then he would not be saying that he had organised joint action with them but he would be in command of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, Colonel Milanovic proposes, in Prosecutor's Exhibit 537, to General Krstic, he makes this proposal: "To authorise and appoint the Commander of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade as commander of all forces which are participating in the searching of the terrain and sweeping the battlefield." Now, General, that is the order which General Krstic told this Court that he approved of that proposal. So you would agree with me, on the basis of that, General Krstic believed that he was appointing the Commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade as the commander of all of these forces including the MUP and the 65th Motorised Protection Regiment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Continued]
utterances.text: I cannot answer the question as to what Krstic had in mind when he said that, but what I can tell you is that Krstic could not have authorised the Command of the Bratunac Brigade to have command over the 65th Protection Regiment because he never received any authority to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think perhaps now would be a good time to finish for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Cayley. Mr. Cayley, are you aware of the time that you still have left? Do you know that? According to our calculations, we need to finish or, rather, you need to finish tomorrow before the big break, that is, around noon, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, you have my word that I will be finished by then. I'm as desperate as anybody else to get finished, but I need to get through my material. I have that obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. We should like to do everything we can to complete the testimony of General Radinovic tomorrow, which means that we must be ready to work a little longer, perhaps half an hour longer tomorrow. I don't see there is any resistance, but I assure you that we're about to leave on holiday. I see a smile at least. I don't know whether the smile was provoked by the mention of "holiday" or by prolongation. Anyway, but Madam Registrar, bear in mind that if necessary, we must be ready to work half an hour longer. So for today, General Radinovic, we will stop there and we will resume tomorrow in the hope that we will complete your testimony. So we meet again tomorrow at 9.20. Have a good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
